newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr sags under weight of rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr sags under weight of rate worries.

text.p: The Australian dollar sagged more than 1/3 cent through a slow Monday session as the weight of worry over eroding yield premiums undermined support.

A subdued batch of domestic housing and producer price data provided further reason to fear another cut in official rates here, while the U.S. market was all but pricing in another Federal Reserve tightening following robust data there.

Traders were also alert for any fallout from Friday's slump in U.S. stocks and bonds, noting that similar selloffs in the past had forced some leveraged funds to cut speculative positions, like those in the A$, to cover equity losses at home.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the pressure had bent the currency to US$0.7815/20 from an early US$0.7855/60 and US$0.7857/62 late here Friday.

Support at US$0.7835 had held for much of the session but a late burst of offshore selling cracked it and left traders braced for a test of 78 in the short term. Further bulwarks were put at US$0.7775, which marked the low point of a pullback on Thursday, and the six-week trough of US$0.7735 reached Tuesday.
The major resistance level at 79 cents had hardly been troubled and looked like a being the ceiling for the currency for some time to come, analysts added.
Traders said bulls were pinning their hopes on rumours of a large A$ buy order from a U.S. corporate beneath 78 cents supposedly related to the sale of a Victorian power station.

A station is indeed due to be sold -- details may even be announced this week -- as part of the State privatisation plan and the main bidders are largely U.S.-led. The State government has been talking of a price as high as A$5.0 billion implying the winning group will need to buy a lot of local dollars.
Traders cautioned the price was probably overstated and some deals in the past were partly financed here in Australia, but felt the uncertainty alone could support the currency.
Such assistance was needed given that the currency's interest premium over the U.S. dollar had been eroded by last month's hike in Fed rates and speculation of another on the way.

The risk of a domestic easing had not entirely faded either and more data like today's on mortgages could make it a reality. Commitments for housing finance fell 6.9 percent in February in a correction to robust gains the previous two months. The result much in line with the 8.0 percent fall the market had already braced for and had little impact.
Analysts noted the weakness was exaggerated by a sharp pullback in refinancing activity, after months of strong growth.
They also suspected a problem with seasonal adjustment factors and looked for a bounce back in March.

"It is still reasonable to expect some acceleration over the next few months as very low interest rates feed through into the mortgage market," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia. "We are still confident of a lift in dwelling investment through the course of 1997."

But neither did the data suggest the economy was anywhere near overheating, particularly as it came hot on the heels of a dismal March employment report which showed plenty of slack in the labour market.
The lack of inflationary pressure was reinforced by data on manufacturing output prices for February which showed a modest 0.2 percent gain taking annual growth to just 0.6 percent.
This was the tenth consecutive month where annual growth was under 1.0 percent reflecting in part intense competitive pressures and the dampening effect of the higher dollar.

This boded well for another slowdown in consumer price inflation when the March quarter figures are released on April 23. Analysts are still fine-tuning their forecasts but generally expect the key underlying rate to rise 0.4 percent on the quarter taking the annual rate to 2.0 percent from 2.1 in Q4.
The headline rate will slow even further as the effects of lower interest rates feed through and could well fall to around 1.1 percent from 1.5 in Q4.

And analysts fully expected this impressive performance to last through 1997 and into 1998, meaning the scope was there for the Reserve Bank to ease policy again should it feel the economy needed a further push.

On the crosses the local dollar succumbed to 98.59/69 yen and 1.3414/27 marks from 99.12/22 and 1.3516/32 late Friday. In trade weighted terms it was steady at 60.8 but the close was recorded before its late slide. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
